findings.title: Group member pagination total page count is incorrect
findings.body: `totalPages` is calculated as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For member counts that are an exact multiple of the limit (for example 50 members with a limit of 50), this returns one extra page. The UI will show an incorrect page count and allow navigating to an empty page. It should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` with a zero-count guard.

findings.title: Public group members endpoint has unvalidated pagination parameters
findings.body: The public members endpoint uses `params[:limit]` and `params[:offset]` without type coercion, bounds, or non-negative validation. A client can pass a very large limit and force serialization of the entire group membership, causing resource exhaustion. Negative limit/offset values can produce invalid SQL errors, and array-style params such as `limit[]=1` can raise because `Array#to_i` is undefined. The values should be coerced to strings/integers and clamped to a safe range.

findings.title: Adding group members fails for usernames with surrounding whitespace
findings.body: `add_members` splits the comma-separated usernames but does not strip each token. Input like `"user1, user2"` produces `" user2"`, which will not match a username and is silently ignored. The parameter should also be coerced to a string, and each username should be stripped before lookup.

findings.title: add_members returns success even when unknown usernames are skipped
findings.body: The action silently ignores usernames that do not match a user and still returns `success_json`, even if none or only some of the requested users were added. The client has no way to know that the operation did not fully succeed. Invalid or missing usernames should be reported in the response.

findings.title: Breaking change to group members JSON response shape
findings.body: The members endpoint previously rendered a serialized array of users, but now returns an object with `members` and `meta` keys. Any existing client or plugin expecting a top-level array will break. If this change is intentional, it should be called out/migrated because it is a public JSON API contract change.

findings.title: Group update treats missing visible parameter as false
findings.body: `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally assigns the attribute. A PUT request that omits `visible` will hide the group, and a JSON boolean `true` is also treated as false because it is compared to the string `"true"`. This can cause unintended visibility changes for API clients performing partial updates.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group test uses the wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The route for removing a group member is defined as DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`), but this spec calls `xhr :put, :remove_member`. The test therefore does not exercise the actual route verb and could mask routing regressions; it should use `:delete`.
